text:
zoe: Noticed parity drift: quickstart calls `sdk.routes.create({ name, visibility: 'private' })` but Node SDK ignores visibility and server defaults to public. Docs/curl show `visibility=private`.

omar: Can you paste the failing repro?

zoe: Quick snippet in sampleapp: `await sdk.routes.create({ name: 'demo', visibility: 'private' })` then `GET /routes/:id` returns `visibility: public`. Error seems to be we serialize `visibility` as `scope` in body for older clients.

rachel: Oof. We recently renamed field server-side from `scope` -> `visibility` but kept backwards compat in REST. SDK serialization used legacy `scope` for compatibility but server prefers `visibility` in the new quickstart path so default applied.

sam: Two quick fixes: 1) patch sampleapp to explicitly set header `X-Route-Visibility: private` in REST fallback while we fix SDK; 2) change SDK to accept both `visibility` and `scope` params and send canonical `visibility` in body, plus a unit test for both variants.

omar: I'll open a small PR that maps `scope` -> `visibility` and preserves `scope` alias. Also add an integration test that creates a route and asserts visibility persists.

rachel: Docs action: update quickstart to note that older SDKs may use `scope` and recommend upgrading. Also add a DX CI gate that runs quickstart create/read checks after SDK upgrades.

devex-bot: Created issue #788: "Node SDK: route visibility param alias and sampleapp parity" assigned to @omar. https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/issues/788 :white_check_mark:

zoe: Deploying a tiny sampleapp fallback that posts directly with `visibility` until SDK lands. Will remove once PR merges.

omar: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/820  adds visibility alias + tests. Requesting review from @rachel and @sam.

sam: Good catch. After merge, let's run a quick audit for other recently-renamed fields to avoid similar drifts.
